thesis: This episode argues that Costco is a highly efficient retailer that prioritizes member value and retention over maximizing margins, a philosophy instilled by its founders. It highlights the company's low overhead costs, achieved through cleverness and efficiency rather than squeezing suppliers, and its ability to pass on supplier price reductions to members. The thesis is supported by claims regarding Costco's membership growth, low selection strategy, and highly efficient cross-dock system.

claims.claim: The host mentions Airbnb as the reason for the hotel problem downtown.
claims.quote: David: I know. Airbnb is the thing.

claims.claim: The host repeats the name of the company.
claims.quote: Ben: Airbnb.

claims.claim: Costco has the lowest prices but the wealthiest consumers of any major retailer.
claims.quote: David: This is one of the most surprising things about Costco. They have the lowest prices, but they have the wealthiest consumers of any major retailer.

claims.claim: For every dollar Costco gets a supplier to reduce the price, the customer sees 89% of the benefit.
claims.quote: Ben: And because of Costco’s gross margins always being targeted at 11% capped at 14%, this means that for every dollar that Costco gets a supplier to reduce the price on something—again, tough but fair—the customer actually sees most 89% of the benefit.

claims.claim: Costco passes 89% of supplier price reduction benefits to members.
claims.quote: or every dollar that Costco gets a supplier to reduce the price on something—again, tough but fair—the customer actually sees most 89% of the benefit. Costco really does just get to pass whenever they get a benefit, 89% of that benefit goes to the member.

claims.claim: Costco prioritizes providing value to members and retaining them over maximizing margins.
claims.quote: The way I look at this is some companies always look for ways to make more margin. Costco specifically does the opposite. They look for ways to provide more value to members, retain them for members as longer, and get them to get their friends to be members.

claims.claim: Costco achieves lower overhead costs through cleverness and efficiency rather than squeezing suppliers.
claims.quote: They look for ways to provide more value to members, retain them for members as longer, and get them to get their friends to be members. They try hard across the board to get lower overhead costs through cleverness and efficiency, not through squeezing, underpaying, or anything like that.

claims.claim: Costco operates as a company that works hard to charge customers less, a philosophy instilled by Jim Sinegal.
claims.quote: Henceforth, as of today, Amazon is a company that works hard to charge its customers less, and that is directly from Jim Sinegal.

claims.claim: Costco has a lopsided relationship with suppliers due to being a massive customer for any given supplier.
claims.quote: But since Costco sells so few items, they are a massive customer for any given supplier. They always have this super lopsided relationship. The average revenue per product because of the SKU count at Costco is about 10 times Walmart.

claims.claim: Costco respects suppliers as one of its four main tenets, even though shareholders are not explicitly listed.
claims.quote: Notoriously missing from these four is the notion of a shareholder. Jim Sinegal articulates, if we do these four things throughout our organization, and again, those four things are obey the law, take care of our members, take care of our employees, respect our suppliers in that order, then we will achieve our ultimate goal, which is to reward our shareholders.

claims.claim: Costco's code of ethics and squeaky clean reputation helped them get the permit to sell alcohol in the mid-80s.
claims.quote: The state had a vested interest in preventing very large retailers from becoming the volume of selling beer and wine. Costco, because they were started with this ethos, came through squeaky clean and actually got the permit. There was literally nothing that you could drudge up on them to deny them.

claims.claim: Costco has a long-term-oriented mindset with a six-year gap between membership fee increases.
claims.quote: I think it's been six years between the last two times they raised the membership, even $5. It's a ludicrously squeaky clean and long-term–oriented mindset.

claims.claim: Costco's house brand, Kirkland Signature, is viewed as an opportunity to provide value to members rather than capture more margin.
claims.quote: I do think, much like their 11% Target gross margin on everything, Costco looks at their house brand as an opportunity to provide value to members, not an opportunity to capture more margin for themselves.

claims.claim: Kirkland Signature sales were $52 billion last year, representing a quarter of Costco's top line.
claims.quote: Certainly, consumers agree, $52 billion of Kirkland Signature sales were done last year. That does not include the Kirkland Signature gas. Out of Costco is 230 billion top line, a little under a quarter of it was Kirkland Signature sales and closer to a third if you include the gas.

claims.claim: Costco's low selection strategy works because they ensure everything they sell is high quality.
claims.quote: Obviously, if you have selection, it makes the life of a retailer very difficult in a lot of ways, but it was just assumed that you had to. But Costco makes the opposite bet. They bet that you don't need selection, as long as you ensure that everything you can buy is high quality. That is the crazy thing that has worked.

claims.claim: Costco has grown membership significantly over the last 25 years, from nearly nothing in the early 90s to $4.5 billion today.
claims.quote: Ben: Yes. In the last 25 years, membership has grown from nearly nothing. If you look at what the numbers were in the early 90s compared to today, $4½ billion.

claims.claim: Costco's membership business takes almost no investment and they don't do any advertising.
claims.quote: Ben: Crazy. Again, David, this membership business takes almost no investment. David: They don't do any advertising.

claims.claim: Costco's two-tiered membership system is illustrative of management's thinking and a microcosm for all of Costco.
claims.quote: Ben: Yes. 1998, the executive membership. What is the executive membership and why are we bothering to spend time on it? Isn't it just a second higher price membership? It is super illustrative of management's thinking, so I love this as a microcosm for all of Costco.

claims.claim: If you hit the $1000 cashback limit, it means you're spending $50,000 at Costco a year.
claims.quote: Ben: Right. If you actually hit that $1000, it would mean you're spending $50,000 at Costco a year.

claims.claim: The break even point of the $60 executive membership is $3000, which is not that hard to hit.
claims.quote: Ben: The break even point of this $60 is $3000, which is not that hard to hit. In fact, it's right around, and I suspect this is why management price is that way, it's right around the average household spend at Costco.

claims.claim: If you get the Costco-issued Citi Visa card, you renew at an even higher rate.
claims.quote: Ben: If you get the Costco-issued Citi Visa card, you renew at an even higher rate.

claims.claim: Costco is the third largest retailer in the US behind Amazon and Walmart.
claims.quote: Ben: Right, and you're the third biggest player in the largest market, America behind Amazon, and Walmart.

claims.claim: Costco's business model of low selection and high quality works because it simplifies operations and drives efficiency.
claims.quote: Costco makes the opposite bet. They bet that you don't need selection, as long as you ensure that everything you can buy is high quality. That is the crazy thing that has worked.

claims.claim: Costco's cross-dock system is highly efficient, with 92% of merchandise cross-docked compared to only 10% for Walmart.
claims.quote: Just to underscore how differentiated the system is, 92% of Costco's merchandise is crossdocked. Only 10% of Walmart has crossdocked merchandise on a pallet system like this.

claims.claim: Costco generates over $730,000 of revenue per employee due to its efficient alignment of trade-offs.
claims.quote: This is why they generate over $730,000 of revenue per employee. They're just efficient in aligning their trade-offs.

claims.claim: Costco is an amazing business to own despite having only 11% gross margins because it drives significant volume and operating income.
claims.quote: Even though Costco is only an 11% gross margin business and only ever will be an 11% gross margin business, it's still a pretty amazing business to own.

claims.claim: Membership fees represent about 70% of Costco's operating income, while retail contributes the remaining 30%.
claims.quote: It is accurate to say that membership fees represent about 70% of the company's operating income with the other 30% of the profit margins coming from retail.

claims.claim: Membership fees represent about 70% of the company's operating income with the other 30% of the profit margins coming from retail.

claims.claim: Costco has decided to only be a decent return on invested capital retailer, which allows them to have an insane return on invested capital membership club business.
claims.quote: I basically think that Costco has decided to only be a decent return on invested capital retailer, which allows them to have an insane return on invested capital membership club business.

claims.claim: Costco is a $230 billion company that none of the other big companies can copy.
claims.quote: co is a $230 billion company that none of the other big companies can copy. Walmart is trying and still is not succeeding at it.

claims.claim: Costco has developed a lot of counter positioning power as a huge incumbent.
claims.quote: David: Yup. I think where they've ended up is actually in a pretty good place and in a better place, I think, than Walmart. That place being that, no, no, the whole point is we are not an ecommerce company.

claims.claim: Costco has latent branding power and latent scale economies, choosing not to recognize short-term profits.
claims.quote: Ben: In a lot of ways, I think what Costco is doing is, they realize that they have latent branding power and latent scale economies. They choose not to recognize short-term profits from those.

claims.claim: Costco trades at a much higher multiple than Walmart because of durability and the membership model.
claims.quote: David: Totally. Let's just say, I don't think we've talked about market cap yet. Costco does $240 billion in revenue today? Ben: Yup, and Walmart does $620 billion.

claims.claim: Costco is uniquely positioned to do well in any economic climate, including recessions and booms.
claims.quote: David: Costco, I think, is pretty uniquely positioned in that they're going to do well (I think) in any economic climate. In a recessionary environment, they're going to do well because they are the lowest priced retailer of goods out there.
